main_issue: Whether Agent D, vegetarian for a month, can keep taking part in the dinner rota by cooking his own portion separately (before 6.30) on others' nights, versus the rota needing everyone to eat the same single meal.

A-B.evidence: A insists the shared meal is the point (T22, T27); B says D cooking before 6.30 works and asks 'What is the actual problem?' (T21, T23, T26).

A-C.evidence: Early both objected that it defeats the rota's point (T7, T9, T11). C later accepted cooking before 6.30 (T18), while A still objects (T27).

A-D.evidence: D proposes cooking separately before 6.30 (T10), asks A what to do (T19); A keeps saying it isn't a shared meal (T13, T16, T27).

B-C.evidence: B (T14) and C (T18) both say D cooking before 6.30 is fine; C initially objected to simultaneous cooking.

B-D.evidence: B asked about kitchen space (T6), then accepted the before-6.30 plan (T14) and defended it against A (T21, T23, T26).

C-D.evidence: C objected to simultaneous cooking (T9); D offered to cook before 6.30 (T10) and C accepted: 'that's fine with me' (T18).
